statement: I know what my business is worth today, based on a credible recent valuation, not a guess or a rule of thumb.

levels.label: No real idea
levels.description: No real idea, I'd be guessing.

levels.label: Rough guess or rule of thumb
levels.description: A rough gut number or an old rule of thumb.

levels.label: Recent informal estimate
levels.description: A recent informal estimate or calculation.

levels.label: Credible formal valuation
levels.description: A credible, current formal valuation.

statement: Have you determined the specific after-tax amount you need from the sale of your business to fund your retirement,  and how confident are you in that figure?

levels.label: No number
levels.description: No number. Haven't quantified what the sale needs to net you.

levels.label: Gut-feel target only
levels.description: Gut-feel target only. Not calculated, not tied to retirement spending, ignores taxes.

levels.label: Calculated but not updated
levels.description: Calculated after-tax target based on a real retirement plan, but not recently updated or stress-tested.

levels.label: Validated and stress-tested
levels.description: Validated, current after-tax number built with an advisor, tied to a documented plan and stress-tested against downside scenarios.

statement: How much runway do you have before you’d like to step back or transition out of the business?

levels.label: Less than 3 years
levels.description: Less than 3 years, or I don't know yet.

levels.label: 3 to 5 years
levels.description: 3–5 years.

levels.label: 5 to 7 years
levels.description: 5–7 years.

levels.label: More than 7 years
levels.description: More than 7 years.

statement: I have a plan for how and when I'll hand off or sell the business.

levels.label: No plan
levels.description: I don't have a plan.

levels.label: Written down
levels.description: I have one and it's written down.

levels.label: Shared with wealth advisor
levels.description: I have one, it's written down, and it's shared with my wealth advisor.

levels.label: Shared with all advisors
levels.description: I have one, it's written down, and it's shared with all my advisors and they're meeting regularly to talk about it.

statement: Our accounting team produces accurate monthly financials on a timely close.

levels.label: Late, unreliable close
levels.description: One bookkeeper (or an outside service) handles everything; books close late, if monthly at all, and I'm not confident they're accurate.

levels.label: Slow or inconsistent
levels.description: In-house bookkeeper with outside CPA support; statements come eventually, but slow or inconsistent.

levels.label: Trusted, regular close
levels.description: An in-house controller closes the books monthly on a regular schedule, and I trust the numbers.

levels.label: Fast, diligence-ready close
levels.description: In-house finance leadership (controller and CFO) with a team; accurate monthly statements on a fast, predictable close.

statement: How would you rate your company’s budgeting and forecasting process, including how regularly you compare actual results to budget and update forecasts as business conditions change?

levels.label: No reliable budget
levels.description: No reliable budget or forecast; limited tracking against actuals.

levels.label: Annual, occasional review
levels.description: Annual budget with occasional actual vs. budget review.

levels.label: Monthly variance review
levels.description: Monthly variance reviews and forecasts updated periodically.

levels.label: Rolling forecasts
levels.description: Rolling forecasts updated regularly and used to guide decisions.

statement: If a buyer showed up tomorrow, do you think you could deliver meaningful information to them in a timely manner while maintaining the appropriate level of confidentiality?

levels.label: Would need a lot of help
levels.description: No, we'd need a lot of outside help just to pull the information together.

levels.label: Would be a scramble
levels.description: Eventually, but it would be a scramble, and keeping it quiet would be hard.

levels.label: Most within a few weeks
levels.description: We could produce most of what's asked within a few weeks, with some help.

levels.label: Three years within two weeks
levels.description: We could hand over three clean years within two weeks, quietly, without disrupting the business.

statement: I have someone financially capable I trust to work on a confidential deal without alarming the rest of the staff.

levels.label: No one I'd trust
levels.description: No one, inside or outside that I'd trust with confidential deal work.

levels.label: Not sure they could handle it
levels.description: Maybe someone internally, but I'm not sure they could handle the workload.

levels.label: Capable trusted person
levels.description: I have a capable, trusted person in-house or an outside advisor.

levels.label: Briefed and ready
levels.description: I have a trusted, deal-capable person already briefed and ready to go.

statement: What's the highest level of externally reported financial statements?

levels.label: Internal only
levels.description: None. Internal only.

levels.label: CPA compiled
levels.description: CPA compiled financial statements.

levels.label: CPA reviewed
levels.description: CPA reviewed financial statements.

levels.label: CPA audited
levels.description: CPA audited financial statements.

statement: Does my team have the bandwidth to take on deal work on top of their regular job?

levels.label: No
levels.description: No, they're already stretched.

levels.label: Some
levels.description: They could absorb a little extra, but something else would slip.

levels.label: Most
levels.description: They could handle it for a few months, with some outside help.

levels.label: Yes
levels.description: Yes, my team could take this on and keep the day-to-day running.

statement: How concentrated is your business among key customers and vendors?

levels.label: One customer over 50%
levels.description: One customer or critical vendor is more than 50% of the business.

levels.label: Top customers 30 to 50%
levels.description: Our top customers or vendors are 30–50% of the business.

levels.label: Top customers 10 to 30%
levels.description: Our top customers or vendors are 10–30% of the business.

levels.label: No customer over 10%
levels.description: No single customer or critical vendor is more than 10% of the business.

statement: How dependent is the business on you or other key individuals to operate successfully?

levels.label: Relies heavily on me
levels.description: The business relies heavily on me, if I were unexpectedly out for an extended/indefinite period, it would have a hard time continuing to operate successfully.

levels.label: Some dependence remains
levels.description: The business could keep running without me for a period of time, but certain important decisions, relationships, or responsibilities still depend on me.

levels.label: Strong team, still relied on
levels.description: I have a strong management team that can run the business, but I’m still relied on for certain key decisions or relationships.

levels.label: Runs smoothly without me
levels.description: I could step away from the business for a month and it would continue running smoothly without me.

statement: How well are your internal processes documented?

levels.label: Little written down
levels.description: We have very little written down, most processes live in people’s heads

levels.label: Documented, not consistent
levels.description: We have some processes documented, but they aren’t consistently followed or tracked.

levels.label: Documented, not measured
levels.description: Most of our key processes are documented and generally followed, but we don’t consistently measure performance against them.

levels.label: Documented and measured
levels.description: Our key processes are clearly documented, consistently followed, and measured using defined KPIs.

statement: What percent of your revenue is recurring?

levels.label: Almost none
levels.description: Almost none, we start from zero every year.

levels.label: Less than 25%
levels.description: Less than 25% of our revenue repeats.

levels.label: Roughly 25 to 50%
levels.description: Roughly 25–50% of our revenue repeats.

levels.label: More than half
levels.description: More than half our revenue repeats or is under contract.

statement: How much of your day-to-day data and reporting is automated versus manually updated across different systems?

levels.label: Mostly manual
levels.description: Most updates are manual, and our systems don’t really talk to each other.

levels.label: Some automation
levels.description: Some things are automated, but we still rely heavily on manual updates and moving information between systems.

levels.label: Mostly connected
levels.description: Most of our key systems are connected and automated, with some manual work still required.

levels.label: Well integrated
levels.description: Our systems are well integrated, and information flows automatically with very little manual effort.

statement: I know which jobs, products, or customers make me the most money, and which ones lose money.

levels.label: No clear view
levels.description: We don’t have a clear view of which jobs, products, or customers make or lose money.

levels.label: General sense only
levels.description: We have a general sense of what’s profitable, but it’s not consistently backed by data.

levels.label: Track profitability
levels.description: We track profitability and can identify our strongest and weakest jobs, products, or customers.

levels.label: Detailed and actively used
levels.description: We have detailed profitability data by job, product, or customer and actively use it to make business decisions.

statement: How would you rate your ability to understand your cash flow?

levels.label: Limited visibility
levels.description: We have limited visibility into cash flow and are often surprised by cash needs.

levels.label: Understand current position
levels.description: We understand our current cash position, but future cash needs can still catch us off guard.

levels.label: Regularly forecast
levels.description: We regularly forecast cash flow and generally understand when and why cash needs will arise.

levels.label: Reliable and proactive
levels.description: We have a reliable cash flow forecast, understand the key drivers behind it, and proactively plan for future cash needs.

statement: How well do you track and benchmark your key financial and operating KPIs, including margins, against targets and industry standards?

levels.label: Don't track consistently
levels.description: We don’t consistently track key KPIs or know how our margins compare to benchmarks.

levels.label: Limited benchmarking
levels.description: We track some key numbers, but benchmarking is limited and we don’t always know what is driving changes in performance.

levels.label: Regular tracking
levels.description: We regularly track KPIs and margins against targets and benchmarks, and usually understand the reasons behind variances.

levels.label: Actively benchmark and use it
levels.description: We actively benchmark our KPIs and margins, understand exactly what drives performance, and use that data to make operating decisions.

statement: How effectively do you monitor and control costs across the business?

levels.label: No cost-control process
levels.description: No real cost-control process.

levels.label: Reactive only
levels.description: We keep an eye on costs, but mostly react when something looks too high.

levels.label: Regularly track costs
levels.description: We regularly track costs against budgets or expectations and address issues when they arise.

levels.label: Disciplined process
levels.description: We have a disciplined cost-control process that identifies variances early and drives corrective action.

statement: How clearly are your personal and business finances separated?

levels.label: Frequently mixed
levels.description: Personal and business finances are frequently mixed together.

levels.label: Mostly separate
levels.description: They are mostly separate, but there is still some overlap.

levels.label: Clearly separated
levels.description: They are clearly separated, with only occasional exceptions.

levels.label: Fully separated
levels.description: They are fully separated, with clear accounts, records, and processes in place.
